title: Remembering Sir Patrick Stewart's Video Game Roles
hook: Sir Patrick Stewart died on October 28 at 86. Before Oblivion players ever left the sewers, his was the voice that sent them on their way. Which of his roles will you remember most?
script: Did you know Sir Patrick Stewart was one of the most familiar voices in gaming? He died on October twenty-eighth at his home in Los Angeles. He was eighty-six. Most people knew him as Captain Picard or Professor X. He played both of them in video games too, across many Star Trek and X-Men titles. But for a lot of gamers, his biggest moment came in two thousand six. In The Elder Scrolls Four: Oblivion, he voiced Emperor Uriel Septim the Seventh. The emperor is only with you for the opening of the game, escaping through the sewers before he is assassinated. Even so, his calm and steady voice is the first thing that sends players off on their journey. When Bethesda remastered Oblivion in twenty twenty-five, they kept his original performance. In two thousand ten, he played Zobek in Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. He returned to the role for the sequel in two thousand fourteen. He also narrated the War of the Worlds game and the indie game My Memory of Us. His family called him a son of Mirfield, in the West Riding of Yorkshire. Thank you for the voices, Sir Patrick. Rest well.
